acts.26.p1.b1.text: “You have permission to speak for yourself.”

acts.26.p1.b2.text: Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

acts.26.p1.b3.text: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,

acts.26.p1.b4.text: … I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

acts.26.p2.b5.text: … I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.

acts.26.p2.b6.text: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,

acts.26.p2.b7.text: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

acts.26.p3.b8.text: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

acts.26.p3.b9.text: … I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.

acts.26.p3.b10.text: … In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

acts.26.p4.b11.text: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

acts.26.p4.b12.text: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, …

acts.26.p4.b13.text: … ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?

acts.26.p4.b14.text: It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

acts.26.p5.b15.text: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.

acts.26.p5.b16.text: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness …

acts.26.p5.b17.text: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, …

acts.26.p6.b18.text: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

acts.26.p6.b19.text: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, …

acts.26.p6.b20.text: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

acts.26.p7.b21.text: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike.

acts.26.p7.b22.text: I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

acts.26.p7.b23.text: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”

acts.26.p8.b24.text: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice,

acts.26.p8.b25.text: “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”

acts.26.p8.b26.text: “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.

acts.26.p9.b27.text: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. …

acts.26.p9.b28.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”

acts.26.p9.b29.text: “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
